newsitem.title: UK: West of Shetlands Clair crude in refinery tests.
newsitem.headline: West of Shetlands Clair crude in refinery tests.

text.p: Crude oil produced at the Clair field west of the Shetland Islands is undergoing refinery tests to determine quality and refined product yields, said a spokesman for operator British Petroleum Co Plc.
But BP has not yet decided on how to proceed with the field because it is unclear whether commercial production levels could be sustained, the official said.
BP recently completed an extended well test at Clair which tested well flows of more than 15,000 barrels per day (bpd), industry sources said.

"The tests have gone reasonably well. But we want to make sure we can get sustained production from it. There is plenty of oil down there, but now we have to do some number-crunching," a BP official said.
Like other grades from West of Shetlands fields, Clair is heavy and sweet, oil analysts said.
The BP official said it was too early to determine the product yields and quality of the Clair crude, but testing at the refineries should provide some information.
"When Clair was first discovered it was considered heavy, and this heavy label stuck. It may be heavier than other North Sea grades but not as heavy as originally thought," the official said.
Oil consultants Arthur Andersen said the main uncertainty with Clair was the reservoir complexity and performance.

Clair was discovered 19 years ago but tests have yet to provide sufficient information on flow potential and sustained production that prove the field could be developed commercially, oil analysts said.
Foinaven, the first field to be developed in Britain's Atlantic waters west of Shetlands, is expected to start production some time next year.
